title: The Hope in Her Heart
subtitle: A single candle's light cannot fill an empty room.

items.text: The Hope in Her Heart
The council chamber on the fifth floor is nearly overflowing.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: I never would have expected so many arcanists to risk their lives for the Foundation, even with their powers taken away from them.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: You underestimated them, just as you've always underestimated what solidarity can accomplish.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Solidarity? I never thought I'd hear that word coming from you.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen—
An authoritative voice from the podium puts an end to their bickering.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Inside this room are all the surviving members of the Committee and the House of Integratus.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The third floor of the Committee Building has fallen, and the enemy is advancing through the fourth as we speak. If this continues, the entire building will fall before help arrives.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: The president has ordered an immediate evacuation. All of you and any other non-combatant staff are to head to his office on the top floor.
Constantine steps down from the podium. The solemn silence of the room is interrupted by the not-so-distant hammer of gunfire beyond the door.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Look at us. A bunch of beaten-down cowards.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Hah. And who do you intend to hold accountable this time?

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Gentlemen, please, choose your battles.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Yes, we used to fight over policies in this room. But now is the time to set our issues aside and unite around our common goal.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Survival. Yes. That is the grim reality.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: I had hoped we might reconcile under better circumstances.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Don't lose hope yet, Pedra. Perhaps one day we'll be able to return to this room more united than ever before.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: We can save the debate over that until we get out of here in one piece. Every second we linger is another stress on the people protecting our lives.
Nautika tumbles through the air.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Hold on tight.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Nautika!
The impact of her landing rumbles the ground like a burst of artillery.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I-I took as much of the impact as I could. Are you alright?
Her lower body has faded and crumpled like loose fabric. No matter how Nautika tries, her beast half lies still and unresponsive—an exhausting, fruitless struggle.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Yep, everyone's okay.
They all climb down from Nautika's back.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Uh, we woulda been toast without you, Nautika. You good?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm just glad no one's hurt. But I-I need some time to get up.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: What just happened? Is everyone alright?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Huh? Didn't you feel loopy when Arcana did that hush trick?

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Loopy? I didn't feel a thing.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Maybe it only affects arcanists.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I can't use any of my arcane skills. It's like the channel of my pneuma is blocked.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Like a clogged pipe?
He casts aside his doubts for now and looks around.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Whatever it was, the enemy will be hunting for you. Stick with us. We humans don't need powers to fight. Alright team, gather up.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Yo, Cap, don't you go treating me like some kinda pushover. My blade still cuts, with or without my arcane skills.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Wouldn't think of it, J. Just don't get yourself hurt, alright?
"Razor" rallies those who can still fight.
Just as they're circling around Nautika, a moth appears and lands on Eagle's shoulder.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: A moth? Ms. Stranger, is that you?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I've found clues as to the Manus entry point.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Operation's going smoothly so far. Entrance should be located and closed down in no time.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Is she saying she's found the Manus entry point and she's on her way to close it?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: That's what I heard too. But ...
Another possibility tugs at Eagle's mind.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: How did this message get through? All arcane skills are muted. Only the Manus can …

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Did she ...?!

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: *cough*
Her mouth is pried open and the struggling moth flies out.
It returns to Ms. Stranger's ear to whisper memories and information and then disappears.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Looks like the risk paid off. The mask restored my power.
Viscous slime drips from the mask and onto her pale cheeks.
The ritualist slumps against the wall as if utterly drained, though no more worse for wear than "Grace."

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You dare to steal power from a Manus mask. Are you brave or merely foolish, Grace?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: This isn't the first time I've been tested by it, Prima. I know how to resist its corruption.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: Your resistance is meaningless. The mask will destroy the unfaithful. But you've lived on stolen time for long enough. I should've ended you before you ever made it to Antarctica.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Is that so? Funny. I always thought you were more eager for your mother's death than I was. You wanted her position for yourself, didn't you?

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: You lie!

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I have only ever admired her unwavering devotion to the Guiding One.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: A devotion that ended in martyrdom—a sacrifice which shall be rewarded. Her-Her flesh may have perished, but her name lives on.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: As for you, treacherous pest that you are, you will die inconsequential and unremembered.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Inconsequential ... That sounds familiar. They did tell you what happened during your mother's so-called "martyr's death," didn't they?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It wasn't some sacred act. She wasn't chosen. It was an accident, Prima.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The roof collapsed. A large chunk of it fell, and she was too absorbed in her own preaching to notice, until it squashed her like a bug.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: An inconsequential, meaningless death. The only good thing that came of it was the silence.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: No. Damn you and your lies!

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Do you really think her death meant anything to Arcana? None of you have ever mattered to her.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: She sent you here to spread chaos simply because it amuses her. She calls herself a savior, but she doesn't care if any of you die in the process.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Because she isn't a savior, nor a god. Only a purveyor of lies and chaos. All she brings is ruin and death.

items.speaker: Ritualist
items.text: I ... I'll tear that blasphemous tongue from your mouth!

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Descend   into   dreams.
The ritualist succumbs to her exhaustion and falls unconscious. Ms. Stranger, hearing the faint murmurs coming from the mask, turns around.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Both the Manus and the Foundation lie for our loyalty and sacrifice.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: But whatever lies they tell, it makes no difference to me. I am loyal only to my own cause now.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: My Semi-Automatic Construction Arm has gone offline.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Leave it. Laplace's equipment runs on arcanum. They'll all be useless now.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Human soldiers, behind the barricade. Cover the arcanists as they retreat, now!
All that's left along the path of the soldiers' retreat are bizarre tools.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Looks like we're doing this the old-fashioned way.
Their arcane skills may have faltered, but their bullets still fly. Though the tide has turned against them once more, the Foundation continues to resist in every way they can.
A soldier trains his sights on this wholly exposed target.
She advances without hurry, without fear, through the hail of fire. The soldier's finger finds the trigger.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Hold your fire.
A hand grips his shoulder.

items.speaker: Soldier I
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: All units, hold fire. That's Arcana. Firearms don't harm her. Disengage, I repeat, disengage!
Creius has no particular authority to issue orders, but as glimmers of recognition spread through their ranks, they take heed of him all the same.
Meanwhile, Arcana continues toward the Foundation's line of defense, unbothered by the display.

items.speaker: Arcana
items.text: Ah, guns. How quaint.
She strolls past their defenses as one might a garden hedge.
For a moment, every soldier present can feel the heartbeats of their neighbor throbbing in their ears, until the gunfire resumes.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: She warned me about this.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Why didn't she do anything, sir?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Because we're irrelevant to her.

items.speaker: Foundation Security
items.text: Then, what do we do?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: All we can do—slow down the rest of the Manus forces. Leave Arcana to those who can handle her.
His eyes betray his confident tone as he stares out at the smoke-filled hall. Eventually, his gaze turns to his hand.
Several minutes ago, a moth sent by Ms. Stranger had landed there.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Ms. Stranger, you were right about her.
